brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 4 full bases on level 0 + 4 on level 1 with solid top covers (cover:-1,0,1;full;top etc.) forming a 2-storey shelf deck (f23 ~453x310mm). Staged with book-stack and book-row props visible in look.

Configurator checks fit/collisions only; parts are 3D-printed plastic with user-chosen material. No load testing, material strength or kg rating is modelled or verified. Shape provides flat shelves but cannot be claimed as 50 kg rated.
Two notch drawer frames installed: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 and notch:0#0,-1#notch4, each provides pull-out drawer storage in lower storey.

finish.summary: Built 8-cell two-storey shelf unit with capped faces and locked joints, topped with solid covers as shelves and dressed with books. Installed two notch drawers. Load rating cannot be verified - 3D-printed system does not model or test weight capacity, so 50 kg rating is unmet.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
